newsitem.title: USA: U.S. deficit seen falling sharply this year - CBO.
newsitem.headline: U.S. deficit seen falling sharply this year - CBO.

text.p: The U.S. budget deficit is expected to fall sharply to $11 billion for the first nine months of fiscal 1997, down from a $74 billion deficit in the same period a year earlier, a Congressional Budget Office analysis said Thursday.
A strong economy has propelled higher-than-expected tax receipts into the Treasury and reduced the deficit faster than expected.
The CBO, in the analysis dated July 9, estimated a $54 billion surplus for the month of June. The analysis was based on May Treasury data of government revenues and spending.

"Receipts continued to be quite strong in May and June, while outlay growth slowed," the CBO analysis said. "A $54 billion surplus is estimated for June, lowering the cumulative deficit for the first nine months of fiscal year 1997 to $11 billion, down sharply from the $74 billion deficit last year for the same period," CBO said.
Fiscal 1997 started Oct. 1 1996 and ends Sept. 30, 1997.
The U.S. economy grew at a 5.9 pct annual rate in the first three months of this year but is forecast to have slowed to about a 2-to-2-1/2 percent pace in the second quarter.
Wall Street analysts have forecast the deficit could fall to below $50 billion by the end of fiscal 1997, and some said the deficit could be wiped out as early as next year.

The improvement in the deficit has come at a time when Congress is trying to patch together legislation to implement a five-year budget agreement reached with the White House in May. That pact aimed to erase the deficit by 2002.

White House Budget Director Franklin Raines Wednesday said economic strength could not alone eliminate the deficit and that the budget agreement was necessary. He called "absurd" some notions that letting current fiscal policy continue on "automatic pilot" would be better for eliminating the deficit than implementing the budget agreement.
The White House Office of Management and Budget postponed its mid-session review of the budget until after the budget legislation is completed.
